title: RawTransactionEvent
description: CONTRACT 1 of 3. Emitted by the producer (stage 1), validated at stage 2, consumed by the scorer (stage 3). One card transaction replayed from the Sparkov dataset as a live event. Frozen at v1.0.0 — any change must be announced to the whole team and the version bumped.

schema_version.description: Bump only by team announcement. Validation rejects anything else.

event_id.description: Generated fresh by the producer on every emit. NOT the dataset's trans_num — a replay of the same row produces a new event_id, which is what makes load-test runs distinguishable.

emitted_at.description: RFC3339 UTC with milliseconds. THIS IS THE LATENCY CLOCK START. End-to-end latency is defined as committed_at (Postgres) minus emitted_at. Set it at the instant of emit, not at the top of the loop iteration.

run_id.description: Optional tag for a load-test run, e.g. 'loadtest-2000eps'. Carried through to Postgres so results can be reported per run. Defaults to 'default' downstream if absent.

source_trans_num.description: The dataset's trans_num. Traceability back to the CSV row.

occurred_at.description: From trans_date_trans_time, KEPT AS-IS with a 'Z' appended — do NOT shift the clock. '2019-03-02 14:17:00' becomes '2019-03-02T14:17:00.000Z'. The dataset timestamp is naive; treating it as UTC preserves hour-of-day, which is a real fraud signal. Converting from an assumed local zone moves every hour and breaks that feature. This is 2019-2020 dataset time, NOT wall-clock emit time — never use it for latency.

unix_time.description: DERIVE FROM occurred_at, do not copy the CSV's unix_time column. Because occurred_at is the naive dataset clock labelled Z, the CSV's own unix_time is offset from it by whatever zone the generator assumed — copying it makes the event internally inconsistent, and datetime.utcfromtimestamp(unix_time) would not round-trip back to occurred_at. Kept because velocity features are cheaper to compute on an int.

card_id.description: EXACTLY sha256(<cc_num as plain digit string>).hexdigest()[:16]. The scorer uses this to recognise returning cards for velocity features, so any other derivation silently breaks scoring. READ cc_num WITH dtype=str — pandas infers it as int64 or float64, and a float turns 4999891557932452 into '4.999891557932452e+15', which hashes to a different value for every row. The raw cc_num never enters the pipeline.

card_last4.description: Display only. Never a model feature.

amount.description: From amt. USD, 2dp. Max is a sanity bound well above the dataset's real max (~$28,949) so real rows never hit the DLQ by accident.

category.description: DELIBERATELY NOT AN ENUM. The 14 known Sparkov values are entertainment, food_dining, gas_transport, grocery_net, grocery_pos, health_fitness, home, kids_pets, misc_net, misc_pos, personal_care, shopping_net, shopping_pos, travel. Do not enum this until someone has run df.category.unique() on the actual CSV — a wrong enum value sends every matching row to the DLQ.

cardholder.description: Cardholder context needed for geo-distance and demographic features. The dataset's first, last and street columns are DROPPED AT THE PRODUCER and never appear here — synthetic or not, name-and-address does not belong on a shared cloud instance, and saying so out loud is worth a point with a judge.

zip.description: STRING, zero-padded to 5. The CSV parses zip as an int, which silently drops the leading zero on every New England ZIP. Read it with dtype=str or zfill(5) at the producer or you will DLQ thousands of valid rows.

label.description: GROUND TRUTH. Segregated from transaction/cardholder on purpose. Carried so the dashboard can show live precision and recall, which is a strong demo. HARD RULE: the scorer (stage 3) must not read this object. Anything under transaction/cardholder is a legal feature; anything here is not.
